title: JVM Memory: Heap vs Stack Demystified

scenes.say: Ever wonder why the JVM splits memory into heap and stack? Let's break down what matters most for your interview.

scenes.label: Heap
scenes.sub: Stores objects, managed by garbage collection.
scenes.say: First up, the heap. This is where your objects live, and the garbage collector keeps it tidy.

scenes.label: Stack
scenes.sub: Holds method calls and local variables, per thread.
scenes.say: The stack is different. Each thread gets its own stack for method calls and local variables. It's fast, but limited in size.
Heap is shared and managed by garbage collection, but it's slower. Stack is thread-local, much faster, and gets cleared automatically when methods return.

scenes.question: Are objects stored on the stack?
scenes.wrong: Yes, small objects can be on the stack.
scenes.right: No, all objects go on the heap. Stack only holds references and primitives.
scenes.say: Here's a classic trap: Are objects ever stored on the stack? Nope. Only references and primitives live there. Objects always go on the heap.
